summary.title: Summary
paragraphs: Software engineer with {{OVERALL_EXPERIENCE_YEARS}} years of experience designing and shipping production web applications, real-time systems and cloud-native products. Since 2022 at XBO.com, building the real-time trading frontend of a crypto exchange. Strong in TypeScript, React, Node.js and AWS.

Outside XBO, builds AI products and agent systems end to end: co-founded ELI, an AI tutor with paying subscribers; built Mrrlin, a workspace that runs coding agents behind review gates; and built the Hermes-based agent harness that runs ELI's and Mrrlin's email and support operations. Looking for a hands-on Senior or Staff IC role on a product team: product engineering, applied AI and reliable systems.

entries.name: Senior Frontend Engineer · XBO.com, crypto exchange
entries.descr: Architected and built the frontend of an award-winning crypto exchange (Best Digital Assets Exchange 2024, Best Crypto Processing Solution 2025): spot, futures, CFDs and a loyalty program in 10+ languages.
bullets: Real-time data: designed the SignalR/WebSocket data layer with sub-second updates for order books, charts, tickers and positions; RxJS stream handling keeps the UI smooth under high-frequency updates.
Correctness: arbitrary-precision arithmetic for trading calculations; type-safe order forms with real-time validation.

AI-driven delivery: since mid-2026 my work here runs through an agent harness I built around the team's Azure DevOps flow: agents turn user stories into implementation-ready specs, coding agents implement in isolated git worktrees, a multi-model consensus gate reviews the design and every PR, browser QA agents verify acceptance criteria with screenshot reports, and a design QA agent checks the result against Figma.
entries.stack: React, Redux, TypeScript, SignalR, RxJS, Claude Code, Codex, MCP

entries.name: Co-Founder & Engineer · ELI, AI language tutor
entries.descr: AI English tutor for pronunciation and goal-based speaking practice (job interviews, work meetings, relocation). Live with real learners: 52 active paid subscriptions, ~780 users; revenue Stripe-verified on TrustMRR. Owned the technical side end to end: architecture, backend, frontend, AI pipeline, payments, infrastructure, CI/CD.
bullets: Backend & payments: fully serverless, event-driven AWS stack (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, DynamoDB, CloudFront, Cognito) plus GCP Cloud Functions, Firestore and Firebase Auth; Stripe subscriptions with tiers by speaking minutes and webhooks.
AI pipeline: LLM orchestration with LangChain and fine-tuned GPT models; Whisper speech recognition on serverless GPU; phoneme-level pronunciation scoring with real-time feedback.
Learner model: a profile updated after every conversation (weak sounds, vocabulary gaps, progress toward a goal) that sets dialogue difficulty, vocabulary and scenarios.

entries.name: Creator · Agent operations harness (Hermes Agent + Outlab)
entries.descr: Built alone the ops system behind ELI and Mrrlin (mailboxes, support inbox, reply triage): an always-on Hermes Agent does the work through Outlab, a TypeScript service, steered from Telegram channels, one per workflow. In production daily.
bullets: Agent-facing API: Node.js/TypeScript (Hono, SQLite) with leases, claim tokens and idempotency keys, so agents work in parallel without double work; systemd timers, health checks and alerting.
Quality gates: nothing the agent writes goes out until independent reviewer models score it against weighted criteria and hard rules (LLM-as-judge); replies are drafted for human approval.
Integrations: mailboxes over IMAP and the Gmail API, reply triage, ELI's support inbox, Telegram alerts.
Own engineering harness: blind consensus reviews across Claude, Codex and Gemini CLIs before implementation and before every PR; a git worktree per task; handoff state so any agent can resume.

entries.name: Co-Founder & Engineer · Mrrlin, AI execution workspace
entries.descr: Designed and built a workspace that takes one goal and returns finished work by coordinating the coding agents a team already uses. In daily use by our team.
bullets: Orchestration: a Director agent turns a goal into a plan of tasks and routes each one to Claude Code, Codex CLI or another model by task type, with routing aware of subscription usage.
Quality gates: multi-model consensus review sends weak output back for another round; a task closes only with proof: a live URL, a green build or a human sign-off.
Isolation, memory, approvals: every task runs in its own git worktree with its artifacts recorded; decisions go to project memory; one approval inbox, and autopilot stops at approval points.

entries.name: Frontend Engineer → Frontend Tech Lead · robota.ua
entries.descr: Ukraine's largest job board (6.5M+ resumes, 100K+ active listings). Moved a .NET/jQuery monolith to Angular + GraphQL (Apollo) services with a Tailwind design system and built the mobile SPA. As tech lead of the frontend platform: cut CI build time from ~40 to ~20 min (TeamCity to GitHub Actions, incremental builds, caching), moved key pages from red to green Core Web Vitals, introduced TypeScript strict mode, SonarQube and Sentry. Built a serverless GEOHASH-based ETA service for public transport on GCP that reduced Google Maps API costs.
